prompt: You're reviewing a teammate's pull request for a distributed rate limiter. It enforces three nested quota tiers on every request — user, then tenant, then global — checked in that fixed cascade order, and the whole increment-check-reject sequence runs inside one atomic Redis Lua script so no concurrent client can ever see a half-applied state. The author swears it's never thrown or crashed in production, yet the tenant and global counters keep drifting slowly higher than the number of requests actually granted. Read the script below, explain exactly why the counters leak even though nothing errors, and tell the author precisely what to change in each reject branch plus how you'd verify the leak is gone.
givenCode:
-- Distributed rate limiter: cascade of user -> tenant -> global quota tiers.
-- KEYS[1..3] = userKey, tenantKey, globalKey
-- ARGV[1..3] = userLimit, tenantLimit, globalLimit
-- Runs as a single atomic EVAL so the increment-check-rollback sequence
-- for all three tiers is indivisible under concurrency.

local userKey = KEYS[1]
local tenantKey = KEYS[2]
local globalKey = KEYS[3]

local userLimit = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local tenantLimit = tonumber(ARGV[2])
local globalLimit = tonumber(ARGV[3])

-- Tier 1: user quota
local userCount = redis.call('INCR', userKey)
if userCount > userLimit then
    -- only the user tier was incremented so far, so this fully compensates
    redis.call('DECR', userKey)
    return {0, 'user'}
end

-- Tier 2: tenant quota
local tenantCount = redis.call('INCR', tenantKey)
if tenantCount > tenantLimit then
    -- at this point BOTH userKey and tenantKey were incremented above,
    -- but only tenantKey gets rolled back here
    redis.call('DECR', tenantKey)
    return {0, 'tenant'}
end

-- Tier 3: global quota
local globalCount = redis.call('INCR', globalKey)
if globalCount > globalLimit then
    -- userKey, tenantKey, and globalKey were all incremented above,
    -- but this branch only rolls back globalKey and tenantKey
    redis.call('DECR', globalKey)
    redis.call('DECR', tenantKey)
    return {0, 'global'}
end

-- all three tiers within limit; every increment above is legitimately kept
return {1, 'allow'}
